note: Adapted from the species description of Adaiphrotermes choanensis by Sands (1972), originally in English; the species has no soldier, and only the alate and the worker are described; the section on variation at the end of the original account is condensed into one sentence of the diagnostic characters. Measurement-table headings, figure numbers and locality records are not translated, and some measurement values corrupted by OCR in the tables are omitted.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate is extremely variable and was initially divided into two species, later united when intermediates were found; the variation correlates with year of collection: from earlier to later collections the body size increases steadily, the fontanelle becomes increasingly contrasting in colour as the head capsule darkens and changes from concave to projecting, while the compound eye remains relatively unchanged and the head capsule appears broader and rounder behind the eye. The typical form is the larger, darker one with a distinctly raised fontanelle.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule white, pilosity short and fine, pale yellow. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/Ri 2.50–3.40, Pcl/W 0.27–0.34; proximal end of left accessory marginal tooth just free of the molar prominence. Fore tibia inflated, Ti/Tw 3.54–4.00. Mixed segment very long, 7–8 times the width of the midgut at the insertion of the Malpighian tubules; enteric valve seat a sessile circular lip on the second hindgut pouch, completely concealed beneath the rectal folds in dorsal view of the abdomen; internal cushions smooth, without traces of scales or reticulation; membrane beyond the cushions with reduced spines.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule from dark brown to dull dark brown, blackish above the ocelli; fontanelle extremely variable, either very small, circular, slightly concave and concolorous with the head capsule, or larger than an ocellus, white, swollen and elongate-oval; middle spot circular to oval, about one quarter the size of an ocellus, usually slightly raised; postclypeus dark brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark variable, usually distinct, crescent-shaped, without setae, flat; antennae pale brown. Pronotum dark brown, meso- and metanotum brown, without dark sutures; legs, femora and tibiae brown, tarsi pale yellow. Abdominal tergites dark brown, dorsolateral spiracles pale brown; sternites brown with the midline paler, ventrolateral spiracles also brown; cerci yellowish white. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly rounded; ocelli medium-sized, separated from the compound eye by half to two thirds their own minimum diameter; postclypeus medium to large, moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.20–0.30, posterior margin evenly rounded, median suture distinct. Head capsule pilosity slightly uneven, with many long setae, not fully forming a felt, brown.
